newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - June 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - June 24.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Troops resume offensive into northern Tamil rebel heartland after two weeks of consolidation. The advance was temporarily halted after the rebels attacked areas captured by advancing troops.
Police bust racket by separatist Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) guerrillas to send minority Tamil youth abroad using false papers.

A fundamental rights case filed in the Supreme Court on the arrest and detention of Sirisena Cooray, an influential cabinet minister in assassinated President Ranasinghe Premadasa's government, postponed for second time.
Police arrest six people, believed to be LTTE suicide bombers, from Colombo lodging house.

Police expected to take opposition United National Party legislator into custody soon, for allegedly being involved in a plot to assassinate President Chandrika Kumaratunga. Two UNP politicians, including Cooray, are already in custody.
Security forces, who resumed their offensive after two weeks of consolidation, close in on rebel-held town of Puliyankulam.
Government plans to present its devolution proposals to end the ethnic conflict to parliament in early September, parliamentary sources say.
